outcome: Still open in the form the bullet gives: since 26 January 2024 it has moved only for restricted classes (continuous semigroups of disk self-maps, Sept 2024; certain quasidisks, with the preprint first posted 2022 and revised March 2024; univalent rational functions, Dec 2025 and revised to June 2026; basins of attraction at infinity of degree-3-or-higher polynomials with small non-leading coefficients, Apr 2026), and one 2015 preprint with a lower-bound claim was withdrawn by its first author on 13 Aug 2026; no event I found names an AI system.
problem_asks: The bullet, read from its statement: (1) for certain subsets of C, estimate the integral of powers of the modulus of the derivative of a conformal map into the open unit disk. The statement does not name the subsets; the Wikipedia body (not the bullet) fixes them as simply connected open sets W in C with at least two boundary points in the extended plane. (2) The exponent: the bullet gives no exponent. The Wikipedia body states it as: for a conformal map psi of W onto the unit disk, the integral of |psi'|^q over W is finite whenever 4/3 < q < 4. Equivalently, for the inverse map f from the disk onto W, the integral of |f'|^p over the disk is finite for -2 < p < 2/3 (p = 2 - q; this equivalence appears in Aleman and Kouroupis 2024 and Jin 2025). (3) 'Estimating' is the bullet's word; the sources I read state finiteness of the integral and do not give a constant or say whether a bound uniform over W (depending only on q) is part of the problem. (4) The endpoints 4/3 and 4 are sharp per the Wikipedia body and the slit-plane example; this is stated in the body, not the bullet.

events.what_happened: James E. Brennan, 'The integrability of the derivative in conformal mapping', J. London Math. Soc. (2) 18 (1978) 261-272. Formulates the conjecture and proves the integrability for 4/3 < q < q0 for some constant q0 > 3 (Wikipedia body; scilag entry). I did not open the LMS article; the content here is from the two secondary pages.
events.delivers: Formulates the conjecture (finiteness of the q-integral for all simply connected W with q in (4/3, 4)) and proves it for the sub-range 4/3 < q < q0, with q0 > 3 not pinned down in the sources I read. Restricted in exponent only; all simply connected domains are covered by the sub-range.
events.remains: The rest of the exponent range, q in [q0, 4); the full conjecture.

Springer gives 1994 (vol. 32); a Tsinghua archive record gives 1992. I did not open the article.

events.what_happened: Christopher Bishop, 'Quasiconformal Lipschitz maps, Sullivan's convex hull theorem and Brennan's conjecture' (Arkiv for Matematik). One search summary dates it to 2002; I did not verify the year. Bishop shows that if Thurston's K = 2 conjecture holds for a planar domain, then Brennan's conjecture holds for its Riemann map (F' is in L^p for p < 2K/(K-1), which is p < 4 at K = 2). Proving the sharp constant in Sullivan's convex hull theorem would give Brennan in general. Reported in the abstract of Tosic 2022 and in a search summary of the Bishop paper; not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional reduction: Brennan's conjecture for any planar domain on which the K = 2 conjecture holds. Not an unconditional result.
events.remains: Unconditional Brennan for all domains; K = 2 is known to fail for some domains (Epstein-Marden-Markovic, 2004-2005), so the reduction does not reach those domains.

The paper itself was not readable: the Volberg page returned no content and the citation hub has no abstract.

events.what_happened: Haakan Hedenmalm and Serguei Shimorin, 'Weighted Bergman spaces and the integral means spectrum of conformal mappings', arXiv math/0406345 (v1 17 June 2004, the only version); Duke Math. J. 127 (2005) 341-393. Abstract (opened): univalent maps on the disk; a Prawitz inequality and a Mobius map to the bidisk give 'rather strong estimates from above' on the integral means spectrum. The paper's own introduction (ar5iv, read in part) sets a critical value R_CM with 2 <= R_CM < infinity and says the Brennan conjecture is equivalent to R_CM = 2, i.e. the universal spectrum at -2 equals 1. Secondary sources (Aleman-Kouroupis 2024 introduction; Zheng 2026 introduction; Jin 2025 introduction) state that they prove the conjecture for p in (-1.752, 2/3), which is q < 3.752, and Jin calls their bound the current best upper bound on the universal spectrum at -2. I did not find the -1.752 sentence in the text I could read.
events.revisions: v1 17 Jun 2004 only (arXiv); journal Duke Math. J. 127 (2005).
events.delivers: A bound on the universal integral means spectrum over all univalent maps, not a restricted class. Per secondary sources, Brennan's integrability holds for p in (-1.752, 2/3), i.e. q in (4/3, 3.752); the paper's own text gives 2 <= R_CM < infinity and the equivalence of Brennan with R_CM = 2.
events.remains: The range q in [3.752, 4) (p in (-2, -1.752]), and therefore the full conjecture.

events.what_happened: Jianjun Jin, 'On a multiplier operator induced by the Schwarzian derivative of univalent functions', arXiv 2211.01742 (math.CV). v1 3 Nov 2022; v13 19 Mar 2024 (current). arXiv journal reference: Bull. London Math. Soc. 56(7) (2024) 2296-2314 (publication date not verified on the journal site). The v1 abstract (opened) says 'As an application, we prove that the Brennan's conjecture is true for a large class of quasi-disks'. The v13 abstract says 'we show'. v13 full text (HTML, read): Theorem 1.3: if f is univalent on the disk with a quasiconformal extension and ||mu_f||_inf <= sqrt(5/8), then beta_f(-2) <= 1 and Brennan holds for f(Delta). Theorem 3.1: if the boundary dilatation h(f) <= sqrt(3/11), Brennan holds for f(Delta). Remark 4.1: asymptotically conformal f gives Brennan for the quasidisk. Whether the Brennan application was already in v1 is not established: the v1 page I could read gives only the abstract.
events.revisions: v1 3 Nov 2022 (abstract says 'we prove'); v2 6 Nov 2022 through v12 30 May 2023 and v13 19 Mar 2024 (abstract says 'we show'). If the Brennan application was added after v1, the date of that application is the later version in which it first appears; I could not establish which.
events.delivers: Brennan's conjecture for quasidisks f(Delta) that satisfy a dilatation bound (||mu_f|| <= sqrt(5/8)) or a boundary-dilatation bound (h(f) <= sqrt(3/11)), including asymptotically conformal maps. A restricted class of domains; the full exponent range is claimed for each domain in the class (beta_f(-2) <= 1).
events.remains: Every simply connected domain outside that class; the full conjecture.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Aleman and Athanasios Kouroupis, 'Brennan's conjecture holds for semigroups of holomorphic functions', arXiv 2409.15074 (math.CV; also math.CA, math.FA). v1 23 Sep 2024; v2 14 Apr 2025 (current). Abstract (opened): 'we give a short proof of Brennan's conjecture in the special case of continuous semigroups of holomorphic functions', using recent results on Bekolle-Bonami weights and spectra of integration operators. Theorem 1.1 (HTML v1, opened): 'Let {phi_t(z)}_{t>=0} be a continuous semigroup of conformal self-maps of the unit disk'; the theorem gives the integral bound for every p in (-2, 2/3). The introduction states the conjecture for p in (-2, 2/3). Talk abstracts for the Politecnico di Milano seminar (19 June 2024) and a 2025 ULB talk describe the class as 'non-elliptic' continuous semigroups (search snippets; not opened). The June 2024 talk predates the arXiv write-up; by the date rule the event is dated to the write-up. No journal publication found.
events.delivers: Brennan's conjecture, in the p-form, for every p in (-2, 2/3) (equivalently q in (4/3, 4) for the inverse map), for the class of maps determined by continuous semigroups of conformal self-maps of the unit disk. This is a full exponent range for a restricted class of domains; the exact class of domains the theorem covers was not verified beyond the semigroup hypothesis.
events.remains: Every simply connected domain not arising from a continuous semigroup of disk self-maps; the full conjecture.

events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture, on a restricted class with the full exponent range.

events.what_happened: Jianjun Jin, 'Complex exponential integral means spectra of univalent functions and the Brennan conjecture', arXiv 2512.09330 (math.CV). v1 10 Dec 2025 (title then 'Complex exponential integral means spectrums of univalent functions and Brennan conjecture'); v13 5 Jun 2026 (current). Abstract (opened): the author determines the integral means spectra of all univalent rational functions in the unit disk and, 'as a consequence, we show that the Brennan conjecture is true for this class of univalent functions'. Full HTML v13 (read in two passes): Corollary 6.23 gives B(-2) = 1 for the class of univalent rational functions U_R, via Theorem 6.20. The introduction states the general conjecture as open: 'It is conjectured that tau* = -2. This is equivalent to the celebrated Brennan conjecture that B(-2) = B_b(-2) = 1'. The first read of the HTML and a search snippet also say Section 6 covers univalent functions onto bounded polygons; I did not verify that statement in the text.

It depends on the inclusion U_R in L_I union L_II union L_III, which Remark 6.2 states without proof or citation; Remarks 6.15 and 6.18 make similar inclusions without proof, and Remark 6.13 gives a partial sketch.

events.what_happened: Yigang Zheng, 'Brennan Conjecture for Basin of Attraction at Infinity', arXiv 2604.12240 (v1 14 Apr 2026, the only version). Abstract (opened): for any monic polynomial of degree m with sufficiently small non-leading coefficients, Brennan's conjecture holds for its basin of attraction at infinity. HTML (opened): Theorem 1.1, for f(z) = z^2 + a_0 with Omega(f) simply connected, Brennan holds for Omega(f); the paper attributes the degree-2 case to Baranski, Volberg and Zdunik. Theorem 1.4: 'For every m >= 3, there exists delta = delta(m) > 0' such that small non-leading coefficients give Brennan for the basin. No explicit delta is given. Remark 1.2: 'for m > 2 this is not the case', i.e. degree-2 Theorem 1.1 does not cover all degrees. The acknowledgements thank a thesis advisor (Vladimir Markovic) and Haakan Hedenmalm and read as a thesis acknowledgement. No funding, AI or software statement.
events.delivers: Brennan's conjecture for basins of attraction at infinity of monic polynomials of degree m >= 3 whose non-leading coefficients are below a threshold delta(m) that exists but is not explicit. The degree-2 case is the 1998 Baranski-Volberg-Zdunik result as reported in this paper.
events.remains: Polynomials of degree m >= 3 with coefficients above delta(m) (and the explicit size of delta); all other simply connected domains; the full conjecture.

disputes.summary: Best general exponent range. Wikipedia (last edited 30 May 2025) credits Bertilsson 1999 with 4/3 < q < 3.422 and does not mention Hedenmalm-Shimorin. Secondary sources (Aleman-Kouroupis 2024; Zheng 2026; Jin 2025) credit Hedenmalm-Shimorin 2004/2005 with p in (-1.752, 2/3), i.e. q < 3.752, which is wider. I did not confirm the -1.752 value in the Hedenmalm-Shimorin text.
Carleson-Makarov year: 1994 (Springer, Arkiv vol. 32) versus 1992 (Tsinghua archive record).

Jin 2512.09330 and bounded polygons: a search snippet and a first read of the HTML say Section 6 also covers univalent maps onto bounded polygons. The portion of the HTML I read after character 100,000 does not show that statement, and I did not verify it.

Hu and Chen (2015) lower-bound preprint, withdrawn by the first author on 13 Aug 2026 with comment 'Incorrect theorem statement'. The Wikipedia reference list still cites the 2015 arXiv preprint for lower bounds (as of the May 2025 snapshot I read).

summary: Brennan's conjecture is still open in the form the bullet gives. Since 26 January 2024 the problem has moved only on restricted classes, and I found no event that settles the general question. The in-window events are: Aleman and Kouroupis (arXiv 2409.15074, 23 Sep 2024), a full-range proof for continuous semigroups of disk self-maps (Theorem 1.1, p in (-2, 2/3)); Jin's rational-function result (arXiv 2512.09330, first posted 10 Dec 2025 and revised to v13 on 5 Jun 2026), B(-2) = 1 for univalent rational functions, whose key inclusion (Remark 6.2) is stated without proof, and which an automated Pith AI referee (3 Aug 2026) says is 'asserted without proof' in places; Zheng (arXiv 2604.12240, 14 Apr 2026), Brennan for basins of attraction at infinity of degree-3-or-higher polynomials with small non-leading coefficients, where the threshold delta(m) exists but is not explicit and an automated Pith AI referee (10 May 2026) calls the result non-effective; and the withdrawal on 13 Aug 2026 of Hu and Chen's 2015 preprint, which claimed an equivalent reformulation and lower bounds. Two in-window preprints I checked do not state a Brennan result in what I read: Jin's Teichmuller-space paper (arXiv 2405.07683, May 2024) and Jin's multiplier-norm paper (arXiv 2603.16170, Mar 2026). Jin's quasidisk result (arXiv 2211.01742, first posted Nov 2022, journal Bull. LMS 2024, latest version Mar 2024) predates the window, but its last revision is inside it. It gives Brennan for quasidisks with explicit dilatation bounds. Historical events are recorded with dates: Brennan 1978, Carleson-Makarov 1994, Villamor-Xiao 1997, Baranski-Volberg-Zdunik 1998, Bertilsson 1999, Kayumov (2005, 2013), Bishop (2002, conditional on K = 2), Hedenmalm-Shimorin (2004, Duke 2005), and Tosic's 2022 numerical check on the Epstein-Marden-Markovic domain, which is not a proof. The best general range before 2024 is, on secondary sources, Hedenmalm-Shimorin's (-1.752, 2/3), not Bertilsson's, and the Wikipedia article has not caught up. No AI system is named in any event. The AI search (see search.queries) found no AI-linked Brennan result, and the full text of the in-window papers I read for acknowledgements (Aleman-Kouroupis, Jin 2512.09330, Jin 2211.01742, Zheng) has no AI, LLM or software statement. The only AI in any record is the automated Pith reviews, which are recorded under checked_by and are not involvement in the mathematics. Close calls: (a) whether a complete exponent range for a restricted class (Jin 2025; Aleman-Kouroupis 2024) counts as settling any part of the bullet, given the bullet asks about all simply connected domains; (b) whether Zheng's non-explicit threshold is a real restriction in practice; (c) whether Jin's rational-function result stands given the unproved inclusion in Remark 6.2, which I could not confirm either way.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a larger reading: Jin's 2025 preprint gives B(-2) = 1 with the full exponent for a named class (univalent rational functions), and Aleman-Kouroupis gives the full interval (-2, 2/3) for their class, so each could be read as having settled the conjecture for a class in full. Against that, the bullet asks about all simply connected domains, and a restriction to a class of maps is not a change in the quantity it names, so these are restricted cases. A second reading treats the withdrawn Hu-Chen preprint as no event at all; it is recorded because it was posted and was on the record in 2015-2026.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The proof, or the citation for the proof, of the inclusion U_R in L_I union L_II union L_III in Jin 2512.09330 (Remark 6.2, Remarks 6.15 and 6.18), together with Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3 and whether Theorem 4 bears on Corollary 6.23; a human referee report or a journal decision on that paper. (2) An explicit or effective delta(m) in Zheng 2604.12240, Theorem 1.4, or a human review of it. (3) The exact sentence in Hedenmalm and Shimorin (Duke 2005) that gives the range p > -1.752. (4) The text of Bertilsson's 1999 thesis for the 3.422 figure, and whether Wikipedia's statement of it is current. (5) The v1 text of Jin 2211.01742 to see whether the Brennan application first appears there or later. (6) Whether the rest of the work on the bounded-polygon statement of 2512.09330 exists. (7) For the AI question, a full-text arXiv search for Brennan together with the names of AI systems, and the lab announcements and Erdos-problem trackers in full, not only through search snippets.
